private_note: I have a one-in-five chance of each group, so I'm weighing the average against the worst case. Alder keeps the average at 100, the same as Today, and lifts the bottom from 22 to 32 while costing the top only about 4%. It beats Today in nearly every respect. Cedar's higher average doesn't make up for a 15k floor with no health coverage. Hazel and Birch give up 20% or more of the average, which is too much. We need 9 votes, so Alder is the realistic compromise.
statement: Fellow delegates, none of us knows which fifth we will land in, so each of us is betting on one draw. Alder is the safest good bet. On average it pays exactly what we have today, 100 thousand, so nobody's expected income shrinks. Its floor rises from 22 to 32, and everyone gets guaranteed health coverage, so a bad draw no longer means poverty without care. In return, the top fifth gives up only 10 thousand. Cedar has a higher average, but one draw in five leaves you on 15 thousand with no coverage. Birch and Hazel protect the bottom, but they cut the average by a fifth or more, and four draws in five would be worse off than today. We need nine of twelve, or we're stuck with today's system for a generation. Alder is the plan that both those who fear risk and those who want growth can accept. I urge you to rank it first.
